title: Better datetime support in TinyDB (issue #5)
summary: The issue is a vague wish with no concrete behaviour, so the verdict is DRAFT. It names three pain points: converting dates to strings and back, hacky date comparison in queries, and wanting this "out of the box". It does not say which date types, whether the change is automatic or opt-in, what on-disk format to use, or how existing data and timezones are handled. The repo shows the current behaviour: `tinydb/storages.py:147` has `JSONStorage.write` call `json.dumps(data, **self.kwargs)` with no date handling, so inserting a `datetime` with the default storage should fail with a `TypeError`. Dates must therefore be hand-converted to strings, and queries can only compare them as strings. I did not run this. I wrote 3 stated functional requirements and 1 constraint, all NEEDS-CLARIFICATION, plus 2 candidate requirements. Three P1 questions should go to the maintainer first: type scope, where the feature lives, and how values are read back. Stakeholder mode is `unavailable` and no maintainer comments were supplied, so nothing is CONFIRMED. No tool-answerable questions exist (nothing public is named), so no tool calls were made. The issue contains no embedded instructions.

requirements.source_quote: I always end up converting things to strings and back myself

open_questions.question: Which date/time types must be supported: datetime only, date and datetime, or also time and timedelta? Are timezone-aware values in scope?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides the scope of FR-DATE-001, 002 and 003 and the acceptance criteria that use specific types.
options: (d) any of the above, naive and timezone-aware
open_questions.proposed_default: (b), recorded as ASM-002 (PROVISIONAL); it narrows 'dates' only if the maintainer wants times or timedeltas.

open_questions.question: What does 'out of the box' mean, and where should the feature live: automatic in the default JSONStorage, an opt-in option or middleware shipped in TinyDB, or only a documented recipe or extension? Does it apply to other storages (MemoryStorage, custom ones)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides the user-facing mechanism and whether current behaviour changes by default. Blocks CON-DATE-001 and the storing and reading FRs.
options: (b) opt-in bundled middleware or storage argument
open_questions.proposed_default: No default: maintainer decision required (design-level scope choice).

open_questions.question: When reading, should stored date values be returned as Python date/time objects, and how should a string the user inserted that merely looks like a date be treated (left as string, or converted)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether values round-trip as the same type and avoids silently changing user strings. Blocks FR-DATE-002 and FR-DATE-003 and affects FR-DATE-004.
options: (a) only values that were inserted as date objects come back as date objects (a type marker is stored)
(b) any ISO-8601-looking string is converted on read
(c) values come back as strings and only queries understand dates
open_questions.proposed_default: (a), recorded as ASM-005 (PROVISIONAL). It narrows 'converting back' to type-tagged values.

open_questions.question: Which query comparisons are required: <, <=, >, >=, == against date/time objects; ranges; same-day matching on a datetime; comparison against strings; or dedicated helper methods?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 'Comparing dates in queries' has several readings (TERM-004); AC-3 of FR-DATE-003 cannot be written without it.
options: (d) also accept ISO strings as arguments

open_questions.question: What on-disk representation is required, and must existing database files that contain date strings stay readable and unchanged?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides backward compatibility and interoperability with other tools reading the JSON file.
options: (a) ISO 8601 strings with a type marker
open_questions.proposed_default: No default: maintainer value needed. Existing files remaining readable is provisionally ASM-003.

open_questions.question: How should timezones be handled: preserved on round trip, normalised to UTC, or left naive? What should happen when a query compares a naive value with an aware one (Python raises TypeError)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Affects correctness of reads and queries and FR-DATE-005.
options: (d) raise a clear error on mixing

open_questions.question: Who has decision authority over scope: the maintainer, as the issue author? Is the issue author a maintainer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: There is a single requester, so this is not P1, but every question here needs an owner to answer it.

open_questions.question: What should happen on a value that cannot be handled, and should the user documentation get examples?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Edge case and documentation refinement; blocks nothing yet (dimensions 3 and 12).
open_questions.proposed_default: (a) plus a docs example, recorded as ASSUMED with no requirement.

assumptions.text: The issue author or repository maintainer is the decision owner and the only requester.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Answers to questions may come from the wrong person and have to be redone.

assumptions.text: 'dates' includes at least datetime.datetime and datetime.date (provisional default for Q-001).
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Wrong type scope leads to missing or excess behaviour for date, time and timedelta.

assumptions.text: Existing database files with date strings must continue to load unchanged.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Either a breaking change goes unnoticed, or needless compatibility work is done.

assumptions.text: Timezone-aware datetimes keep their UTC offset across a round trip.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Timezone data may be lost or normalised unexpectedly.

assumptions.text: Only values inserted as date objects come back as date objects; ordinary strings are never converted.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: User strings may be silently converted, or date round trip may not work.

assumptions.text: Query support means the standard comparison operators against date/time objects.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Range or same-day queries expected by the author would be missing.

out_of_scope: Choosing a design or implementation (middleware vs. storage subclass vs. query helpers, serialisation format)
Third-party extensions or other storage back-ends, unless Q-002 brings them into scope
Time-series or calendar features such as recurrence, durations arithmetic, indexing or sorting by date
Migration tooling for existing database files (undetermined; see Q-005)
